reviews.text: Payne and his team recreate the early 1970s in such meticulous fashion that you could be forgiven for thinking the film was actually made 50 years ago.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: I didn't know anything about this film but was completely floored by it. I was happily surprised by this story; the performances, script, and message. We don't get movies like this anymore so I'm very appreciative of this.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: One of my favorite films in recent memory. Between the memorable script, performances, and overall look of the film--I loved every bittersweet moment of this film.
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Featuring a winning trio of actors all giving scintillating performances, The Holdovers marks a stunning return to form for Alexander Payne.
reviews.author: William Stottor

reviews.text: In a time when things often seem so hopeless, when the same forces of inequality and military injustices plague our own world, perhaps it’s this film’s realistic salve that makes it resonate so strongly.
reviews.author: William Mullally

reviews.text: Despite the anxiety and even sadness its story exudes, it’s a movie so in love with its characters, and so steadfast in its humanist convictions, that it reaches into your soul and melts even the most frozen of hearts.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: The Sideways actor-director duo combine once again for a terrific, bittersweet rumination on life, love and grief.
reviews.author: Gautam Sunder

reviews.text: Giamatti and Payne are a movie match made in heaven
reviews.author: Jericho Tadeo

reviews.text: Payne crafts a movie about the human condition and the loveliness and messiness that goes with it.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Unfortunately, The Holdovers really lives up to its name. ... Worth seeing for its playful homage to a very specific slice of cinema history, for its three lead performances, and for a few very good scenes that come before those last, long 30 minutes.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Overstreet

reviews.text: Randolph takes the pain and the imminent grief that her character is feeling to the core, making her chain-smoking adaptation to the situation, while watching the game shows and interacting with the other characters all the more impactful.
reviews.author: Jaylan Salah

reviews.text: Absolutely nothing new happens in Alexander Payne’s surprisingly warm and fuzzy film, but it’s a perfectly fine way to while away 135 minutes. And — who knows? — you might even remember some well-worn yet valuable life lessons.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: Anchored by Giamatti’s compelling central performance ..., The Holdovers takes a meaningful dive into a complex world of emotional conflict
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: "The Holdovers" should become a holiday movie classic for audiences to return to every Thanksgiving to keep some perspective on human nature, hypocrisy, and the importance of having a warm heart and a calm mind.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: A small-scale gem that, by utilizing a 1970s setting, manages to recall the intimate cinema of that period.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Giamatti’s performance is a pleasure to watch. He is the presiding presence in the movie, and David Hemingson’s erudite screenplay allows him free range to deliver long lines of invective.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: It's the beautifully-written characters and the actors that inhabit them that will surely receive the most plaudits
reviews.author: Kevin Wight

reviews.text: A new American classic.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: In a film that manages to be touching and consistently funny, you won’t be surprised to learn that a rapport develops between existentially miserable Paul, who seeks solace in Jim Beam and Marcus Aurelius, and prickly, troublesome Angus.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Giamatti doesn’t let Paul’s character tics, which include a prominent lazy eye, to distract from the more subtle aspects of his performance.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: The film is a throwback to the soul-stirring narratives of 70s movies. There’s a lot of attention to detail as it immerses the audience in a time of societal shifts and cultural upheaval.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: The three leads work well together and you will root for them, although there is a predictability and heavy-handedness to the story that makes it less moving than it would otherwise be.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: The warmth with which Payne shows the humanity in his characters helps each one of them unfold into a real, complex person.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: [Giamatti, Sessa, and Randolph] are as unforgettable as this film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: The movie is supposed to uplift and suffuse you in a warm Christmas glow, but Payne’s manipulations are fundamentally cynical—and barely conceal a core of self-satisfaction and cruelty.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: The protagonists of The Holdover are the type of characters that have populated Payne's previous films: creatures overwhelmed by their social environment, who are not denied the possibility of learning and redemption. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: A pleasant, digestible film and the three leads are appealing. ... It is not a genuine advance for the director. The comedy-drama’s general trajectory and ultimately heartwarming denouement are set out for all to see virtually from its opening sequence.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: A straightforward yet effective enough piece of holiday viewing.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: A humorous yet profoundly moving film that explores how devastating it is to create distance between ourselves and the people or things that hurt us. Paul Giamatti delivers his best work, Da'Vine Joy Randolph is a wonder and Dominic Sessa is a true find.
reviews.author: John Rocha

reviews.text: Part of the charm of The Holdovers lies in Payne’s ability to transport viewers back to 1970 without relying on cheap nostalgia.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: If 2024 might finally break the stranglehold of franchise storytelling, may The Holdovers be the harbinger of what's to come.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: Payne's film builds a drama that is as exciting as it is edifying. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a wonderful time capsule, a story out of time filled with lovable characters and Paul Giamatti at top of his game (as usual)
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: The leading actors complement each other wonderfully as their characters find comfort in one another: there's agony, decency and tenderness from a heartrending Randolph; a believable redemption arc for the superb, Scrooge-esque Giamatti.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: A beautiful movie that's required viewing of the season or any other time, Paul Giamatti deserves every accolade. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: The dialog keeps us laughing, even as the underlying emotional realities hit us with surprising resonance.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: The format may be unsurprising but there is nothing unsurprising about just how good and enjoyable this is... this is the kind of bittersweet, character-dialogue driven piece they just don't do anymore.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: [Giamatti] first tightens this thwarted, knotty little man to the point of comic indignation, then loosens and unravels him with such skill that, by the end, the little man doesn’t seem so little after all.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a pleasant, cute film that does not deceive the viewer. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: It is the genius of Paul Giamatti to make us, over the course of this great movie, not just re-evaluate and learn to respect this mess of a man but actually... to love him.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: There’s a bracingly astringent bleakness under its surface layer of melancholy humour; a biting, sharp edge that counters the occasional lurch towards sentimentality.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: The performances from the trio are pitch perfect with plenty of humour and heart — and they soon find themselves going on a life- changing adventure together.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: It’s funny and soulful, and Giamatti is sublime as a man hiding behind his own popularity.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Those hoping for another Giamatti masterclass here will more than get their money's worth. He's better than he was in Sideways. But here's the thing: Randolph and Sessa are every bit as brilliant.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: It’s a masterclass in meshing screenwriting, acting, cinematography and music direction in a seamless blend.
reviews.author: Helen Hawkins

reviews.text: Payne’s bittersweet life lesson doesn’t disappoint.
reviews.author: Stefan Kyriazis

reviews.text: The Holdovers emerges as a testament to Payne's unique storytelling ability, offering a grownup drama for intelligent audiences, inviting a nuanced exploration of the complexities of human relationships against the backdrop of cruel classist rigidity.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Watching The Holdovers is like settling down with a nice mug of mulled wine and a box of chocolates.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: Easy to accuse this of being Alexander Payne in Hal Ashby drag, but this has the beautiful essence of The Last Detail in its bones: bitterly funny, deeply sad, and just hopefuly enough without seeming false or cloying.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: While it’s bound to become a new staple in the Christmas movie canon, the fact is filmmaking as note-perfect and beautifully calibrated as this can be enjoyed any time of year.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: Please -- I beg you, make haste to your nearest cinema. The Holdovers has immediately become one of my annual must-watch Christmas movies, and it become one of yours too.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: Some may still baulk at the conventional structure. But conventions emerge for a reason. An absolute treasure. Merry Christmas to you all.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Giamatti gives a wonderful performance here. He roots his character’s frustrations not in cruelty but in misguided desperation -- an eagerness to mould these boys into men better than himself.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: It is both melancholy and funny as these characters develop the capacity to engage emotionally and take off in new directions. It is affecting without ever being treacly or sentimental and the performances are tremendous.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: The holdovers does have some interesting moments, it does have a few perplexing hiccups, but it's still a solid movie.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: A melancholic story of friendship, loss, and three souls who try, but cannot escape what they feel. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Jose Cruz

reviews.text: The film’s hit rate with zingers is quite something; Payne is also not above a Tabasco dash of slapstick.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: An uplifting wonder, The Holdovers doesn’t hold the same shock value as many of this year’s Oscar contenders. However, by telling a humble story full of passion, it stands alongside the best of the bunch.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: The Holdovers sees Alexander Payne return with one of his funniest, sharpest, and most humane comedies to date...
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The benefit of the Yuletide setting is that Payne has gifted us a film intended to be watched every year. It feels like finding an unwatched classic under the tree on Christmas morning.
reviews.author: Lillian Crawford

reviews.text: Striking a disarming balance between heartbreaking and hilarious, and with the brilliant Paul Giamatti heading up a wonderful cast, director Alexander Payne’s 1970s-set story ... is a rarity: an instant holiday classic for grown-ups.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Alexander Payne has balanced The Holdover’s acerbic wit with generosity. So few filmmakers are capable of managing tone the way Payne can.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: …a beautiful, compassionate, funny film about how relationships can bring the best out of human beings at any time, not just Xmas…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: An appeal to understanding and empathy, it’s a heart felt and gut wrenching, albeit hilarious character study...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: A stellar cast of people I wish we could spend a couple more hours with – or, frankly, an entire holiday season with.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: The final 45 minutes of this film are worth four stars. What happens hurts and warms the heart. The three leads are brilliant. Giamatti and Randolph each won a Golden Globe on January 8. Sessa is an actor to watch.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: It's formula, to be sure, especially coming from Payne, who's done this sort of thing many times before. But it's so finely delivered -- so droll and funny and warm -- that it's hard not to succumb to its charm.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: At its core, this is a movie that repeatedly suggests that nobody really loves you, and if they do, they’ll probably die. Chug some vitamin D and get thee to a sunlamp, as this wintertime blues boogaloo may do a number on ya.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: [The Holdovers] makes no pretence about being anything other than a feel-good film but it’s laced with enough wit and sarcasm to keep you in touch with the fact that nobody here is perfect. Far from it.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Payne's best films - Election, About Schmidt, Sideways, Nebraska - have always featured the implosion and partial redemption of insufferable men, and he is on familiar ground here.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: There’s a modesty to The Holdovers that sits in place with the film’s understated mentality, where its dramatic and comedic sensibilities play off each other in a manner that reiterates Payne’s mastery in storytelling
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Fans of Paul Giamatti & Alexander Payne will consider themselves well-served by an unhurried and rewarding film designed for mature cineastes who enjoy films that allow time for characters to actually breathe and evolve into full-blooded, loveable people.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti is a bristly gift as a pariah who learns to open his heart.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: You will laugh and weep with the three broken souls, and come to love them.
reviews.author: Whang Yee Ling

reviews.text: Soulful... I can't recommend this one highly enough
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: A bittersweet and funny drama, the kind designed for elevated family Christmas viewing  and it's also pretty intimate, with rarely more than a few people on screen at the same time and its flashiest moments reserved for 70s-ifying its Boston set pieces.
reviews.author: Lucy Ford

reviews.text: The Holdovers is, among other things, a love letter to how people used to speak in movies: always to each other, never at each other.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Alexander Payne's best film is carried by Da'Vine Joy Randolph who gives the best performance by any actor this year.
reviews.author: Lucas Moore

reviews.text: The return of Alexander Payne excites and deceives in equal parts within its declared and evident endeavor of, precisely, not being deceitful. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: Alexander Payne returns to the simplicity and the emotive in his new film, a story that aspires to become one of the best selections of the Christmas season. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Irene Crespo

reviews.text: Payne puts his characters through a state of continuous change and slow evolution in this study about finding yourself where you least expect it, the value of companionship, and finding your own path... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: We laugh with these characters, cry with them, and just love to be around them. An instant classic.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Alexander Payne keeps the maudlin threat at bay and contributes a successful panoply of '70s and '80s connections, intimations, and influences to the identifiable formula designed to achieve a 'beautiful' film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Antonio Trashorras

reviews.text: The Holdovers will doubtless become an instant Christmas classic, but don’t let that stop you from seeing it any time of the year. The great performances, poignant storyline, acerbic quips and cunning production value are timeless.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: The Holdovers is the warmest film of director Alexander Payne’s career, if not one of his best. Certainly the one I needed at the end of this year.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: Payne, a master of lowkey narratives about average people coming to terms with great changes in their lives, pulls off a rare feat here – a profoundly heartbroken film that will fill you with hope.
reviews.author: Ana Yorke

reviews.text: Nothing about his [Hunham's] and Mary’s and Tully’s stories surprises us, yet we’re powerless to protest, because the movie is just like its characters, and us: Imperfect, and always, always worthy of love.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The original screenplay from David Hemingson is smart, witty and emotionally resonant. Throw in stellar performances by Paul Giamatti, Da’Vine Joy Randolph and newcomer Dominic Sessa, and you have one of the best comedies in recent memory.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Intelligent, caustic, funny, sad, tender, and melancholic... The Holdovers is everything you can expect from an Alexandre Payne film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: Giamatti teams up with Payne to once again create an Oscar worthy film.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: A bitter movie, but it’s not a cynical one. It finds value in the small victories, even if that’s just as small as having someone sit next to you so you feel less alone when you’re completely alienated from the rest of the world.
reviews.author: Mitchell Beaupre

reviews.text: The Holdovers is the Christmas film we never saw coming.
reviews.author: Kit Stone

reviews.text: Miss Da'Vine Joy Randolph whose range shows no boundaries. In his feature film debut, Dominic Sessa  is a revelation and Paul Giamatti is pure perfection.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: The Holdovers is an emotional ride that never feels manipulative. The pacing patient allows every moment and each character time to fully develop. The final moments hit the hardest as the movie cements itself as one of the best movies of 2023.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Muir

reviews.text: Director Alexander Payne (“Election,” “Nebraska”) and television series writer David Hemingson’s first collaboration – shot on location in Massachusetts and set in the 1970s – is an instant Christmas classic.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: [Director Alexander] Payne finds the humor in his most emotionally damaged characters, so his reunion with [actor Paul] Giamatti for the first time since Sideways is a delight.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: This pity party is too transparently allegorical.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: In David Hemingson’s sparkling screenplay, the character development and progression of the relationships is satisfying throughout and a belly laugh or tug at the heartstrings is never far away.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: The Holdovers” has a message that’s realistic, not cloying. It’s treats Christmas not as an excuse to be nice, but as a deeply felt reason to be nice. At its core, it’s about old feelings and new friends. The movie succeeds in every way possible.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: The close observations of privilege and power in The Holdovers are as sharp as anything Payne has delivered since 1999’s Election.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: A brilliant movie that's brave enough to ask the question, "Does Paul Giammati smell bad?"
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: The more we get to know these characters, the more we learn of their motivations, their fears, and their vulnerabilities. The film effectively delves into moral and relationship issues and on the whole is poignant.
reviews.author: Nick Boyd

reviews.text: “The Holdovers” ultimately is Giamatti’s show, and he makes the most of it — creating a detailed character who uses his wit and irascibility to paper over a life of failures and lost chances.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: The Holdovers might be the most perfect Giamatti-delivery vehicle we've gotten in a long time, one that understands that he's best when his talents for yelling are mixed with deep pathos.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: "The Holdovers" fires on nearly all cylinders, though there are moments that drag too much, a byproduct of its unnecessarily lengthy two-hour-thirteen-minute runtime.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Alexander Payne's 'The Holdovers' is a cross between a Christmas fable, with a story of growing up that becomes increasingly strange, emotional and profound. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aglaia Berlutti

reviews.text: At its core it is a dramatic comedy that I find funny and moving when it raises its tone of consistency with its authentic reproduction of the 70s and the splendid performance of Paul Giamatti. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: If you need some holiday consolation, this moving, melancholy film — which is getting some Oscar buzz — could become a new Blue Christmas classic.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Alexander Payne's new film The Holdovers, starring Paul Giamatti, is the kind of wonderful comedy-drama we used to take for granted. Today it feels like a cinematic miracle.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: The Holdovers has a bunch of characters that you love to hate until you don’t. The writers do a great job of making these clichic personas real people with real issues. It is irritating, funny and surprisingly interesting.
reviews.author: Reginald Ponder

reviews.text: ...a deliberate yet increasingly enthralling drama...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: This is Mr. Hunham rediscovering his dignity and purpose, and it is Payne delivering his masterpiece the eighth time out...
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Their circumstances initially seem obvious, but David Hemingson’s script turns in a few twists, leaving in a bit of edge while maintaining an overall sense of warmth—the kind that makes nice holiday viewing.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: Working from a script from David Hemingson, Payne has crafted a wonderful story of loneliness and isolation that manages to be both inspirational and uplifting.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: … you leave the theatre with a renewed sense of what it really means to be human.
reviews.author: Julian Wood

reviews.text: Da'Vine Joy Randolph is amazing in this as well.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: The uncommon movie these days that really does earn laughs and tears.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: A touching drama that infuses acerbic wit with sincere platonic love, convincingly delivered by Giamatti, Randolph, and newcomer Sessa. The comedy is perfectly blended with loneliness, producing a memorable story that can make you laugh and cry.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: The performances by these three lead actors are all superb, and they had to be in order for this movie to work this well with such a small cast.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Whether it’s putting your money where your mouth is or refusing to stay on the sidelines, people make the right choice if their convictions are true, consequences be damned: the essence of being a Barton man.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: There are surprises to be found in The Holdovers, but they come from the characters, not the story — from the ways each of the three main figures reveals new depths and confounds expectations.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: In Payne’s work, one individual’s foibles and failings can open another’s perception; his humans lead not by example, but through their flaws. This is one of the director’s greatest films.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: The way Paul Giamatti tip toes between teacher, paternal figure, friend and even combatant is nothing short of sublime.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Hunham’s hero Marcus Aurelius once wrote, “Give thyself leisure to learn some good thing.” Take his advice and see this film.
reviews.author: Nick De Semlyen

reviews.text: The Holdovers delivers in every way. It is a genuine and heart-warming story with complex characters. Paul Giamatti gives his most memorable performance to date, and this is arguably Payne’s best work.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: There’s something elastic to Giamatti’s performance as Mr. Hunham, particularly in his face: he never lacks a wide-eyed stare or a clenched jaw; it’s a masterpiece of miserly annoyance, he’s the king of put-upon stiffs.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The Holdovers, after being stuck in the snow for too much of its more-than-two-hour runtime, does eventually land in an emotionally satisfying place.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: The best way to describe Payne’s ninth feature is to say it’s remarkably ordinary. A quality that applies to most of his films that are warm, quiet, and inherently funny meditations about unexceptional people leading a simple life.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: There are so many touching and subtle scenes in this film. So well done.
reviews.author: Michael Cook

reviews.text: Alexander Payne has created a wonderful holiday movie about finding a sense of family and caring for others in the least expected places.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Paul Giamati's performance is a master class in acting.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The wit and the warmth just can’t grapple with the overbearing runtime.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Has a new Christmas classic been born? [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: In The Holdovers, Payne has managed to maintain that same keen-eyed insight, but without the sense that the film itself is an active participant in the torment. It’s a rare and remarkable balance to hit.
reviews.author: Melanie Fischer

reviews.text: A wry, artful heart-tugger.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti is a grinchy teacher in Alexander Payne’s loveable answer to The Breakfast Club.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: In heartfelt fashion, however, this festive-adjacent film isn't simply a comedy of teens running amok while Giamatti chases, ruler in-hand. That exists too, but only insofar as it allows us to recognize how similarly damaged Paul and Angus truly are.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Even when the script is hammering home its points, the performances keep the characters multidimensional.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Legitimately one of the best Christmas movies ever made. It's also the perfect Wes Anderson movie for people who don't like Wes Anderson.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: If only The Holdovers had some of its actors’ bonafides. But overall, it feels painfully phony.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: This, for me, is foundational Alexander Payne... It's his best work since Sideways.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: The Holdovers doesn’t miss a beat in examining the sadness churning around the holidays, topping it off with the kind of melancholy yet restorative ending that hits right where it needs to.
reviews.author: Gissane Sophia

reviews.text: Buoyed by a lovingly laid-back pace, gentle dissolve shots and meticulous attention to period architecture, dress, mood and music, "The Holdovers" feels like IT was held over – from 1970.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Before you finish your leftovers, take in 'The Holdovers.'
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: It’s one of those movies that you just want to go on forever because you never want to leave.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Payne has put together a tonally satisfying fable in which people watch each other carefully and wait for them to reveal hidden layers.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: This year’s feel-good winner bubbles with humor and positive change as Payne, transforming an intelligent cerebral script into a captivating film, showcases his storytelling prowess and the power of well-executed, character-driven narratives.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The structure of The Holdovers is certainly a familiar, but Payne dons it like a warm, well loved coat.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Perfectly combines subtle humor, laugh out loud moments, and a chemistry between the two leads that we haven't seen on screen in quite a while. This movie offers up a whole lot of heart, and is a must watch Christmas movie.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti, Dominic Sessa and Da'Vine Joy Randolph give excellent performances in this comedy drama about grief, love and chosen family.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: Giamatti delivers one of his best performances to date, making The Holdovers a perfect family watch despite its very saccharine story.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: It represents a triumphant return to film for Payne after the disappointing “Downsizing,” but it also works (almost) perfectly as a measured, occasionally emotional, beautifully acted drama, shot in a very 70s style. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: The appeal here is in the dialogue (especially Giamatti’s: “Listen, you hormonal barbarian…,” “I find the world a bitter and complicated place – and it seems to feel the same way about me”), the character development, the acting ...
reviews.author: Tim Miller

reviews.text: I absolutely love slice-of-life movies. The Holdovers is one of the best in years.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The snow-covered landscape, Christmas setting, a jazzy folk score by Mark Orton, and wonderful performances by Giamatti, Randolph, and Sessa, make this a must-see! “The Holdovers” is destined to become a cherished holiday classic.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: While The Holdovers conjures warm and nostalgic storytelling with its ’70s found family spirit and trio of outstanding performances — especially Da’Vine Joy Randolph — its emotional impact is stunted by its fractured focus.
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: Call it a return to form or whatever you want. I’ll just enthusiastically say that even with its few minor issues, “The Holdovers” is one of Payne’s best films to date.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: A dramedy about three people reframing sadness and loneliness during the holidays.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Easily one of the best Christmas-themed entertainments in some time because it sustains its brilliance and never resorts to gooeyness.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: [T]his is the movie that Payne’s been hoping to make since his 90s heyday, a film that earns both its jaundiced gaze and its catharsis.
reviews.author: Scout Tafoya

reviews.text: One of the year's best films also makes a strong case for the top spot in director Alexander Payne’s impressive body of work.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Payne’s forte of capturing the humanity in conflicting relationships is apparent in his works. Such is the main drive and the fun found in 'The Holdovers', where we see Payne reunites with Sideways‘s Giamatti.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: I thought it was really terrific and... I think this will be a movie that you'll want to go back to and and revisit.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti [is] so good in the subtlest ways.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Fine performances from Paul Giamatti, Da’Vine Joy Randolph and Dominic Sessa, but something about it left me cold.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Sly in its humor and sincere, though obvious, in its poignancy, human dramas of this sort have become increasingly rare, in the superhero era of cinema. As such, the film may seem better than it actually is.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: There's not a false beat, and it's not a feel-good movie, it's a feel-great one.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: This movie works on so many levels; from the very real and relatable story, Paynes poignant direction, to the beautiful snowy setting, the perfectly placed humor, to the wonderful and world class performances. It’s a delightful holiday instant classic…
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: It starts out like a misanthropic Goodbye Mr. Chips and ends like a pessimist's take on It's a Wonderful Life. But before it's over Alexander Payne's The Holdovers exhibits a humanist's love of its characters.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: While The Holdovers has all of the elements of a period piece, the heart of the film is the same as his present-day tales as it shows Payne’s ability to create smart character-driven social satire.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: It may not be the future of filmmaking, but for two hours at least, the past has rarely felt more present.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: The Holdovers reunites Giamatti with his director from Sideways, Alexander Payne, and he gives what might be an even better performance.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Earthshaking, no, but Payne and company have crafted one of the year's best films, so give yourself an early holiday present and don't miss this humorous, heartfelt paen to compassion for ourselves and each other.
reviews.author: Brian Bromberger

reviews.text: “The Holdovers” is a movie for people who want to spend some time with relatable characters simply trying to navigate the vicissitudes of life. In that, it’s a breath of fresh air.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: ...about the hard, hard work of small acts of kindness.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Like “Green Book,” “The Holdovers” shows us how drastically life has changed, yet emotions haven’t. It's a great trip to the past and a perfect look at how we can improve the future.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: This analog tale with a snappy script and grounded characters provides the warm hug that its audience needs, reminding us that a makeshift family can give a person what they need in the absence of a real one.
reviews.author: Patrick Hicks

reviews.text: Alexander Payne's touching, bittersweet comedic drama is one of the best films of the year. - Director Payne, screenwriter David Hemingson, along with actors Paul Giamatti & Da'Vine Joy Randolph, should score Oscar nominations.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: A genuinely funny and poignant film packed with the qualities of a holiday classic. Payne capably balances comedy and tragedy seamlessly in ways that feel honest and relatable.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: This exactly the type of theatrical film that we were told Hollywood would not be making in the post-pandemic era: a non-franchise, character-driven, middling-budget drama aimed at adults. Thank goodness, at least in this case, the pundits were wrong.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: In its own way, the first runner-up for the coveted "People's Choice Award" at September's 48th annual Toronto International Film Festival actually brings in the 2023 holiday movie season.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: This is a darkly humorous character study into self-isolation and self-destruction that presents the warmth of dysfunction.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Wry, funny (with some zingers that will stay with you long after the film is over), and closely observed, The Holdovers is my kind of Christmas film.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: The Holdovers could make a great play one day. For now, though, it’s just a deeply pleasant movie.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: Stands as a celebration of the quiet, everyday heroism that shapes our lives, reminding us that sometimes the most profound connections are forged in the unlikeliest of places.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Sour but also weirdly cloying, full of sympathy for the working man yet also strangely pretentious. A nostalgic tribute to naturalistic 1970s cinema that somehow completely misses the point of those movies.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: This subliminal familiarity with the theme, setting, and situation decisively contributes to making the audience feel good, along with the ending, which is partially predictable but perfect, and satisfying in every way. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti gives his best performance since Sideways, reteaming with director Alexander Payne for a melancholic Christmas classic in the making.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: In his latest film, Payne foregoes some of his trademark cynicism and goes straight for the heart, resulting in a touching seasonal film for people who aren’t that jazzed about the holidays.
reviews.author: Chad Byrnes

reviews.text: Payne's best since Sideways; the entire ensemble deserves praise for bringing it their all. A lovely, melancholic Christmas story; it almost feels more like a live-action adult version of what Charlie Brown goes through. A must-see for this time of year.
reviews.author: Jim Laczkowski

reviews.text: In the dramatic comedy “The Holdovers,” the director lets in the sweetness just a little bit. And that’s splendid.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Payne and Hemingson have created a well-paced, witty, film with just enough physical comedy for Giamatti and Sessa. We could see The Holdovers become a new holiday classic to be held over year after year.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Giamatti has a ball here as a glass-eyed grump, but he’s a known quantity. The lupine Sessa is the revelation; it’s a gutsy move putting him in a movie theater scene watching Dustin Hoffman, but it’s no accident.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Payne's first-ever period piece is an unconventional holiday film that stars the always-wonderful Paul Giamatti.
reviews.author: Stacey Yvonne

reviews.text: “The Holdovers” is Payne and Giamatti at their very best. A must see, an instant classic, something for everyone.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: For me, it stands as a minor if beautifully crafted film in the context of Payne’s entire oeuvre, but a potential classic of the miserable-holiday subgenre.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Can be thought of as Payne’s response to people who complain that they don’t make movies the way they used to...a funny, insightful film, deeply humane and ultimately quite touching.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Though Giamatti has never not been a joy to see on-screen, he is on another level here, bringing both the necessary comedic timing and dramatic gravitas to hold The Holdovers together.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: A calmly paced movie that allows its characters space to breathe, think and express themselves in their own manner. It’s a narrative not in any hurry to go anywhere but to revel in comedic moments of character.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: An old school slice of comfort and joy for the cold season.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: The Holdovers is perhaps a touch on the schmaltzy side, but it earns that schmaltz through great performances, a sharp script, and a director with an eye for finding beauty and meaning in the ordinary.
reviews.author: Morgan Shaunette

reviews.text: The Holdovers is so good that it’s infuriating that Payne hasn’t made more movies than the eight on his filmography.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: The result mixes charm and smarm in equal measure, never quite resolving into a meaningful exercise, despite the strenuous efforts of all involved.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a brilliant study of an all-boys school and the troubled men it produces.
reviews.author: Annie Berke

reviews.text: Christmas films often deal in the joy/annoyance of family during the holidays, but Payne takes viewers in an entirely different direction in tone and spirit.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Nothing about The Holdovers sounds particularly special, and yet it’s one of director Alexander Payne’s best films -- very funny, occasionally touching and a sterling example of the bonds that can be forged by an unlikely family.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Like Payne’s and Hemingson’s characters, The Holdovers will shift your worldview from meaninglessness into wholesome over 2 hours and 13 minutes. This nostalgic coming-of-age tale delivers a full-circle emotional expedition for young and old.
reviews.author: Robert Butler III

reviews.text: It’s a Christmas movie as uplifting as the saddest of Christmas songs, and as full of hope against all odds.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: A sweet nostalgic character-driven film that is elevated by contrasting personalities that result in well-timed comedic and often, heartfelt humor.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: It could very well have been a recently discovered lost film being released in theaters for all to see.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Characters in The Holdovers have an assortment of disabilities—some of them normalized, but some that border on cliche.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: Alexander Payne has delivered one of the best movies of 2023 - a film you will love to discover and share with others.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: The movie's greatest achievement... is that it has taken a terribly familiar story and has magically managed to tell it in a way that feels fresh and organic, even with the holiday stuff included.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The Holdovers does feel right; its characters feel real, its emotional beats feel earned, and, yes, its faux film grain feels authentic.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: Despite a bit of surprising preciousness, This film is exquisitely performed & its themes of redemption over loss are well played. This has all the requisite wistfulness of a traditional Christmas movie, without any holly jolly. Payne! Giamatti! Reunited!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: It’ll fall into my holiday film rotation, one that the whole family can enjoy without being put off, depressed, or bored. A fresh, impactful, and very funny drama about finding sanity in the unlikeliest of places.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: An incredibly funny and deeply moving film that strikes a damn good balance between coziness and harshness. With a great period setting and fantastic performances. A must see!
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: Yup, it’s a big, gift-wrapped present filled with sentimentality and lovely, effective performances, expertly crafted scenes, and a terrific story.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: Poking fun at the stuffiness and affluence of high-brow academia, this character-driven saga of redemption and self-discovery is bittersweet and quietly profound, sprinkling in nuggets of humane wisdom beneath its familiar surface.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The Holdovers is perhaps a bit on the poky side; little in the story gives much urgency to the pace. But the actors bring their connections to life.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: Audiences will value the time they’re allotted to spend with these characters as they confront some of the most difficult moments of their lives.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: Nearly 20 years after Alexander Payne and Paul Giamatti teamed up for Sideways, they’re reunited for the wintry character study, with Giamatti once again turning in masterful work as a hard-tippling misanthrope...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Finds every avenue to make these characters collide, collude, and refract one another in a dizzying display of heart, humanity, and humor.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: The Holdovers seizes a familiar sensation, one as fleeting as the first snowfall in autumn, and reminds audiences of the emotions that good storytelling can evoke.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: For what might be the finest film of his career thus far, The Holdovers, Alexander Payne has achieved a pitch perfect balance between his trademarked usage of cynicism and sentimentality.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: The movie, like its characters, sometimes seems to be looking for things to do rather than unfolding organically. Still, Giamatti and Sessa hold up their end of the bargain, and Randolph brings a credible sense of pragmatism...
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It’s a very good film, and the best kind of Christmas movie.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The Holdovers manages to be one of those rare movies that asks so little of you, while still giving much ... the message is to throw away your need to analyze, to stop being a nerd and just have fun watching Giamatti struggle to throw a football.
reviews.author: Jackson Weaver

reviews.text: Massachusetts plays itself well enough, but the real joy of “The Holdovers” is watching two pros and a newcomer deliver such beautiful, haunting performances.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: Any warmth The Holdovers gives off is the premeditated kind, like those heating packets you tuck into your mittens on cold days. They’re designed to do the job in the moment. But nothing beats a real fire.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: The Holdovers feels destined to be an alternative holiday classic for anyone who has known the oppressive weight of Christmas loneliness.
reviews.author: Holly Hazelwood

reviews.text: With novelistic detail, Alexander Payne, leading man Paul Giamatti and supporting actors Dominic Sessa and Da'Vine Joy Randoolph make us fall in love with some damaged miscreants at a boarding school near 1970 Boston.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Each scene is a small gem, the ensemble work is as good as it gets, the screenplay by David Hemingson is smart, funny, and touching. This is one of the best films of the year, with career best work by all involved.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a holiday tale with heart, but not the manufactured Hallmark kind that we're used to at this time of the year.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: In “The Holdovers,” Payne finds the perfect balance between comedy and melodrama that he has been searching for his entire career.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: The Holdovers is quite funny ... but the real shock is how genuinely tender and disarmingly warm-hearted it becomes.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a warmhearted coming-of-all-ages movie that never succumbs to cheap melodrama. An uplifting tale of, as Armistead Maupin put it, embracing your logical family instead of your biological one, it avoids overt sentimentality.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The Holdovers is overflowing with gentle warmth and biting humor, making for a perfect Christmas movie and an easy go-to cheer-up picture.
reviews.author: Mark McPherson

reviews.text: Payne brings to the vast tableau of Christmas films a departure — a  movie about  three lonely people having a dickens of a time connecting and dealing with their feelings until they get thrown together to find comfort and joy from each other.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Set in 1970s New England, “The Holdovers” doesn’t only have the look and feel of that time period, it resuscitates the finest elements of its narrative traditions.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: This movie’s religion, if it has one, is the Church of Performance, and Giamatti, Sessa, Randolph and company make it worth attending.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Unabashedly sentimental, defiantly humane, wickedly funny, The Holdovers is a lot like the holidays: a gamut of emotions wrapped up in regrets of the past and uncertainty about the future — tempered by that seasonal dash of against-all-odds optimism.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: We get three actors diving deep into three interesting, nuanced people, and Payne brings us along for the journey.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The calculated silences and cagey revelations result in a movie of truncated characters, with truncated subjectivity, trimmed to fit the Procrustean confines of the script.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Giamatti shines (again) as a crusty teacher watching over a wayward teen.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: It is a film that must be seen in company and that will surely become a classic of the Christmas holidays.
reviews.author: Matías Mora Montero

reviews.text: It does not take a Barton-level scholar to see where The Holdovers is going... but that doesn’t mean there isn’t a tremendous amount of rich, warm, full-hearted fun to be had on the way to the obvious destination.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Giamatti is ably matched by newcomer Dominic Sessa, who holds his own in scenes with the veteran actor and provides the glue that forms the “mismatched buddy” portions of the movie.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The Holdovers might win the award for most WHOLESOME & Delightful movie of the year… A tried and true drama that depicts humanity. Giamatti is GREAT,  Randolph is a standout, but Dominic Sessa is sensational & flat out just won my heart over.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Alexander Payne’s Christmas-set tale of lonely souls is spiced with Giamatti’s performance as Paul Hunham, an acerbically bitter history teacher in an elite early ‘70s boys prep school. In a just world, he will be rewarded with a gold statuette.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: The Holdovers filled a hole in my heart that I often tried to fill by rewatching Dead Poets Society repeatedly. It’s a return to a nostalgic genre that I didn’t realize we’d fully left behind.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: The time and care that Alexander Payne put into this movie pay big dividends. The Holdovers is the best and most satisfying film I’ve seen all year.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: There is perhaps no one better than Paul Giamatti to essay this sort of role. Beetling through each scene with a goodly chip on his shoulder, chafing at school politics, resenting his students, and generally casting a baleful eye on the world at large.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: A heart-lifting story about a makeshift family.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Nothing too cheerful and no one too caustic, apparently this is what’s been missing from the Christmas movie canon: a Payne pop music movie in a minor key.
reviews.author: Angela L. Harmon

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a terrific film with heart and humor and might end up as one of my favorite new holiday films that I don’t think was planned as one.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Destined to become a new holiday classic, The Holdovers is a heartwarming comedy about human connection and the life lessons that really matter. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Absolutely one of the best films of 2023.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: What you do walk away from this cracked Christmas-miracle tale with is an admiration for what Giamatti can do with such flawed people... and how richer we are for having him and Payne give such lost souls such a generous spotlight to grow.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: The Holdovers blends feel-good and sorrowful themes thoughtfully to make a rewatchable flick. But the next watch will likely be over the holidays.
reviews.author: Maxwell Rabb

reviews.text: Like so many of Payne’s movies, it’s about damaged people trying to fashion a new family. I don’t know if all this makes it a 1970s movie or not, but I’m thankful it came out in 2023.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Strong performances make this overly long dry comedy easy to swallow.
reviews.author: Joseph Robinson

reviews.text: It’s a delightful experience overall (sharp dialogue, beautiful performances), even if there isn’t anything in The Holdovers we haven’t seen in previous Alexander Payne movies.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: A warm, spicy brew of humor, poignancy and irascible charm
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti is absolute perfection as a Grinchy teacher who learns a hard lesson in empathy over a winter school break.  All the actors shine in this exuberant movie gift from director Alexander Payne that has all the makings of a new holiday classic.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Payne’s best work seems to come from small ensembles with characters on the brink of completely collapsing. Payne can find the humor and humanity within them.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Perhaps Mr. Payne has gone soft in the two decades since “Election.” Here is an entire school of Tracy Flicks, yet somehow he doesn’t depict them as total monsters.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: Da’Vine Joy Randolph, as Mary, is many things in this platonic triangle. She, though sad beyond belief for her loss, is the anchor that holds the impromptu little family together and allows them to have the best Christmas vacation ever.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: The Holdovers, expanding in theaters just ahead of Thanksgiving, will indeed make for a charming evening with a family that “just wants to see a good film,” but it will never be the picture it thinks itself to be, nor, eventually, a truly memorable one.
reviews.author: Scott Nye

reviews.text: When it’s over, the chill it leaves in your spine is destined to last nearly as long as the smile on your face.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: Little but deeply felt and very lovely.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: This is Payne’s first movie set in any kind of past — it’s using the old M.P.A.A. rating card and was shot, by Eigil Bryld, on cozy 35-millimeter. But it doesn’t feel stuck there.
reviews.author: Wesley Morris

reviews.text: "The Holdovers” means to send you out of the theater exuding holiday cheer and possibly some renewed faith in humanity, but all that lingers, really, is an overpowering whiff of self-satisfaction. It reeks — not of fish, but of insincerity.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Don’t let the wintry backdrop of Alexander Payne’s latest fool you, for The Holdovers is a warm honeyed cider of a film.
reviews.author: Manuel Betancourt

reviews.text: Delivering an abundance of festive charm with its hilarious script, heartwarming story and trio of superb performances, The Holdovers is Christmas at its most comforting.
reviews.author: Hamish Calvert

reviews.text: A trio of great performances, including a never better Paul Giamatti, Alexander Payne perfectly harkening back to the era of 1970s filmmaking and a sharply funny script combine to make The Holdovers one of the best movies of the year.
reviews.author: Michael Balderston

reviews.text: The Holdovers presents a compelling time capsule of an era that may be long ago but still feels raw and relatable today.
reviews.author: Liz Shannon Miller

reviews.text: Filled with acerbic wit and superb talent, The Holdovers is an engaging comedy/drama about finding personal connections with unexpected people. It’s more than a Christmas movie. It’s an authentic portrait of humanity.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a new CHRISTMAS CLASSIC featuring an extraordinary performance from Paul Giamatti. Delightfully charming throughout, it feels like a big warm hug.
reviews.author: Anthony Gagliardi

reviews.text: It tells a familiar story about bonding in the unlikeliest of places but is executed with laugh-out-loud precision, earned emotional beats, and a trio of outstanding performances from Paul Giamatti, Dominic Sessa, and Da’Vine Joy Randolph
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The Holdovers understand that it’s important to find the people in your life who will reinforce good things by being willing to show their flaws rather than constant reassurance despite not giving themselves that grace.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: THE HOLDOVERS is heartwarming, not overly sentimental --- and extremely humorous. It is one of Payne’s very best.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: THE HOLDOVERS is a sweet, frequently funny, slice-of-life story that is not at all maudlin.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: While the movie's tone is comedic, fast-paced, very intelligent, and sarcastic,  little by little, it injects us into the lives of others... It's a movie programmed and intended to make us feel good. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: While there is never any doubt where this film is headed, it’s a lovely, moving story infused with holiday spirit about broken people making each other whole again.  Giamatti is perfection in a role custom tailored for him…
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: If one definition of art is seeing what everyone else does, only in a different way, “The Holdovers” fits that bill. It’s a delight.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: The Holdovers feels like an instant classic, anchored by a knockout performance from Paul Giamatti.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: In a period film dealing with loss and loneliness, Payne isn’t attempting to turn his boarding school-set feature toward tropes of a Dead Poets Society-type drama. He gets much more mileage out of the way two misfits learn to bond on their own terms.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: It lets the viewers' assumptions linger until more information comes up, sometimes only in the background of a larger scene. Life is like that. Answers don't come on a convenient timetable and it is mature of The Holdovers to portray that.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: One of the best scripts in years with 2 masterfully written characters
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: “The Holdovers” feels so distinctly Payne-like that it comes as a surprise that he didn’t write it, or perhaps adapt it from some weird novel that sold eight copies 50 years ago.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Even absent your own memories of smoking indoors or handsewn outerwear, this is the kind of thoughtful, precisely constructed movie where you can almost taste the cigarette smoke and feel your fingers numbing through drafty wool mittens.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Mixing the savory and the sweet, Alexander Payne has given us a gift of a film.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: A warm, wise, and profoundly moving coming-of-age film with just the right balance of humor and heartbreak. Paul Giamatti gives an Oscar-worthy performance.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a mix of melancholy, anger, and humor that feels right for a story set during the holidays, a time which often provokes complicated feelings in people.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: And while The Holdovers does get off to a slow start, the journey is worthwhile, fulfilling, and quite funny.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The Holdovers is among Payne’s best films, largely thanks to its intelligent writing and terrific performances from the three leads.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Writer David Hemingson has crafted an incredibly air-tight, clever, and grounded script that leaves nothing on the table and everything for the taking. The dialogue, glances, and emotional outbursts are earned to a degree that it's almost masterful.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: You’ve seen every aspect of The Holdovers before, from the patter of its dialogue to the bonding that heals its disparate, broken souls.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: A wonderful film, carried by pitch-perfect performances and gorgeous cinematography by Eigil Bryld, putting Payne back on track with another human tale of connection.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti and Alexander Payne reunite for another delectable tragicomedy about a man savoring the bitterness of life -- a school teacher stuck with a challenging student over Christmas holidays.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: The laughs are carried along, though, by a strong undercurrent of sadness as this trio of misfits try to find their way.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: It turns a wintry film into a heartwarming tale about a trio who find a way, by hook or by crook, to get through Christmas together.
reviews.author: Tom Davidson

reviews.text: ... A gentle audiovisual prod in the ribs – reminding the viewer that even though it may be decades out of practice, mainstream American cinema is still allowed to elevate, probe and delight in ordinary lives like these.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: There’s something comforting and soothing about watching these three strangers become a found family, despite their differences and difficulties.
reviews.author: Emily Murray

reviews.text: A shockingly faultless screenplay from David Hemingson exponentially attacks the viewers’ hearts through a truly profound yet bittersweet study of the vital need for human connection. A new Christmas classic is born.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: One of Payne's strongest films in years...it is an unexpectedly heartwarming gem of a film.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: The plot structure may seem familiar but it’s the mood that matters most, as does the gorgeous depiction of complex characters in crisis.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: After the uncharacteristically terrible Downsizing, The Holdovers marks an unequivocal return to form for its director.
reviews.author: Meg Shields

reviews.text: Painfully honest and sentimental, the film strikes a delicate balance of melancholy and humor. It’s like a hug for those who could really, really use one.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: While not the strongest of efforts from Payne, there is certainly a pleasing warmth to The Holdovers that is accentuated by his undeniable sense of craftsmanship and attention to the little details.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: Mixing Goodbye Mr. Chips with Rushmore, The Holdovers is, like its protagonist, gruff yet sweet. For those looking for a Holiday coming-of-age comedy with a spike of melancholy, it'll be the feel-good, feel-bad movie of the fall season.
reviews.author: Christopher James

reviews.text: It’s a lighthearted film on the surface, but themes of grief, loss, and the fear of mortality for teenage boys who know they might be drafted and sent to Vietnam at any moment run beneath the beat of the plot.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Alexander Payne’s The Holdovers is a great movie. It’s easily the most entertaining film he’s ever made, his most through-and-through competent, and one of the best of this year.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: This gathering of three lost souls, pushed together by circumstance and location, takes a bit of time to weave its sardonic magic. But it gets there.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Incorporating Payne's personal experience of boarding school with Hemingson’s script, The Holdovers brings a sense of levity to a teenager imploding.
reviews.author: Nadir Samara

reviews.text: A very solid movie with strong performances throughout. Paul Giamatti is great and his scenes and moments with Dominic [Sessa] really soar.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: Giamatti can do this kind of role in his sleep, but this is one of his best... Sessa, giving his first-ever screen performance, is all raw nerviness, but Randolph might be the film’s most triumphant performance.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: This isn’t a suspense film; it is a character piece, and we’re really here for all those moments in between.
reviews.author: Andy Howell

reviews.text: A simple but thoughtful, heartwarming, charming, and very funny teacher/student story about finding connection, encouraging each other, and learning to be more empathetic. Lovely and perfectly made from start to finish. Give Paul Giammati all the awards.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a terrific Payne film, bursting with sharp laughs and searing sweetness.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Well-acted, lovingly directed [by Alexander Payne], and sharply written by David Hemingson, The Holdovers is a warm, nostalgic hug of a film that harks back to a specific and beloved era of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Emma Badame

reviews.text: There are films that hunt deeper emotions and plenty that just want to entertain. But the best do both. This is what Alexander Payne is about and why he is one of his generation’s finest filmmakers. And The Holdovers is one of his finest films.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: The Holdovers’ difficult character dynamics ultimately fall into all the right places. From beginning to end, Payne’s protagonists often remain static, but their perspectives shift dramatically.
reviews.author: Soham Gadre

reviews.text: Their misery is our gain as filmmaker Alexander Payne reunites with his Sideways star Giamatti for another comedy of thwarted lives that perfectly evokes the 1970s in look, sound and cinematic satisfaction; there’s a fully developed story told here
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Giamatti does some absolutely fantastic work as Paul Hunham, a thoroughly disliked teacher at Barton Academy. Arguably he’s never been better.
reviews.author: Max Covill

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti gives the performance of his career in The Holdovers...This performance is one for the books.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: The Holdovers is ultimately a story about the absence of family, and as it watches three individuals come together and apart, it’s subtly attuned to the way that class constricts people’s lives.
reviews.author: Mark Hanson

reviews.text: A fresh holiday movie that feels light on its feet in spite of its heavier moments and subject matter.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: The first Christmas miracle in the instant Yuletide staple The Holdovers is star Dominic Sessa.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: Neither Payne nor screenwriter David Hemingson are afraid to lean into the romantic notion that three disparate people with vastly different circumstances can briefly come together as a family.
reviews.author: Katarina Docalovich

reviews.text: Despite surface impressions that range from blithely pleasant to genuinely moving or even hilarious in moments, The Holdovers never quite feels effectively or fully conceived, stuck in some nebulous territory.
reviews.author: Jesse Catherine Webber

reviews.text: [A] consistently smart, funny movie about people who are easy to root for and like the ones we know.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Payne’s past films have a stronger strain of social satire than this crowd-pleaser, which predictably lets Hunham lighten up a little through his friendships with a rebellious student, Angus (Sessa), and the cafeteria manager, Mary (Randolph).
reviews.author: Nicolas Rapold

reviews.text: In a career full of excellent Academy Award-nominated and winning work, “The Holdovers” ranks up there with Payne’s very best.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: “The Holdovers” is arguably the feel-good movie of the autumn season that would pair nicely alongside “Dead Poets Society.”
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The movie is a skillfully crafted tribute to the effectiveness of standard coverage when well executed with talented performers, frequently funny while avoiding the unacceptably maudlin...
reviews.author: Vadim Rizov

reviews.text: Despite how tropey it is, it’s an easy-going movie that you can fall under the spell of without much effort.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: [O]ne of the true highlights of the year.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: The Holdovers, while evoking the past, is constantly looking forward.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: It’s the warmest cinematic experience you’ll have all year.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti has never been better, playing a caricatured grump with dynamic and vulnerable layers.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: “The Holdovers” isn’t a return to form for Alexander Payne so much as a concentrated essence of his caustic yet forgiving view of our bumpy, hopeful journey on the road to oblivion.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Funny and rueful, The Holdovers seems beamed in from another time in cinema history, when wordy and thoughtful little movies like this were in healthier supply.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Crushingly wistful in precisely the way moviegoers have come to expect from Payne.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Its sentimentality expertly balanced by its humor, The Holdovers is a story about the lies we tell ourselves (for good and ill) and the reality of our not-so-dissimilar human conditions.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: The Holdovers is proof that we need more thoughtful, studied, loving, and irresistible human stories on screen.
reviews.author: Barry Levitt

reviews.text: Hilarious and heartwarming, this is one of Alexander Payne's best films.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: For how it captures the ambiance of walking out of a liquor store and down a wintry street a few days after Christmas, The Holdovers makes for the ideal annual holiday revisit.
reviews.author: Ethan Vestby

reviews.text: A genial, gentle, redemptive dramedy from Alexander Payne which hits the happy/sad sweet spot with Payne’s sure aim.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a wonderful revelation from an excellent director who proves he’s still able to take us by surprise.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: There might be a sweet 90-minute movie in here somewhere. But as it stands, it’s impossible not to notice how many scenes limp along, how many have nothing to do with the previous one, and how many fizzle out.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti is incredibly moving and Da'Vine Joy Randolph is a revelation in this intimate and moving (while quirky) portrayal of three very different people finding solace for their solitude in each other
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a warm hug of a movie and the closest thing we've had to a new holiday classic in quite some time.
reviews.author: Maureen Lee Lenker

reviews.text: In many ways, though, “The Holdovers” is prestige film comfort food. And that’s meant as a compliment. The movie is genuinely funny.
reviews.author: Gregory Ellwood

reviews.text: Alexander Payne loves to tell stories that embrace and celebrate the power of the human connection. The human connection is the heart and soul of this film.
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: The Holdovers is a return to form for Alexander Payne.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Alexander Payne has masterfully crafted a film that underscores the significance of teachers, both exemplary and challenging, and the profound influence they exert on their students. It’s the kind of film that should resonate with just about any audience.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: It is funny, sad, witty, poignant, filled with snark and heart and great acting. It also manages to be a film set at the holidays that offers something truly new for the genre.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: The vibes are immaculate from the start and only grow more so as the characters gradually start to become as detailed as the world that The Holdovers constructs around them.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Payne, who hasn’t made a film in six years, goes back to basics after the mixed results that was Downsizing, and delivers his best film since Sideways.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: Although it might promptly be added to your holiday movie rotation as a new staple, “The Holdovers” doesn’t exactly feel like a new classic—it feels too familiar for that. Still, it does something tried-and-true so well and affectionally.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Not without its flaws, but it is an engaging and often touching comic drama that builds power as it moves toward its immensely satisfying conclusion.
reviews.author: Stephen Farber

synopsis: From acclaimed director Alexander Payne, THE HOLDOVERS follows a curmudgeonly instructor (Paul Giamatti) at a New England prep school who is forced to remain on campus during Christmas break to babysit the handful of students with nowhere to go. Eventually he forms an unlikely bond with one of them -- a damaged, brainy troublemaker (newcomer Dominic Sessa) -- and with the school's head cook, who has just lost a son in Vietnam (Da'Vine Joy Randolph).
